exposure: maternal age group (young/middle-aged adolescents 13-17 years vs. older adolescents 18-19 years)
cohort: The study included 141 young/middle-aged pregnant adolescents (13-17 years) as cases and 159 older pregnant adolescents (18-19 years) as controls, all from Gadarif Maternity Hospital in eastern Sudan.
finding: Young/middle-aged pregnant Sudanese adolescents were not at increased risk of obstetric and perinatal complications compared to older pregnant adolescents.
mod_finding: There was no significant difference in the rate of cesarean delivery between young/middle-aged and older pregnant adolescents.
